synthesis:draft.headline: AEMO definition of "operational demand"
summary: Operational demand in a region is demand that is met by local scheduled, semi-scheduled and significant non-scheduled generation, by generation from scheduled bidirectional units, and by generation imports to the region, excluding the demand of local scheduled loads and scheduled bidirectional units, and including Wholesale Demand Response. [c1]
The document treats operational demand on a regional basis and states demand can be expressed as actual or forecast. [c2]
Operational demand generally excludes demand met by non-scheduled wind/solar generation of aggregate capacity < 30 MW, non-scheduled non-wind/non-solar generation and exempt generation. [c3]
Actual operational demand includes the measured operational demand reconstituted with estimated actual Wholesale Demand Response (WDR) so historic and forecast operational demand are consistent. [c4]

possible_explanations.statement: Operational demand may exclude small non-scheduled generation as described in the document, which could explain why some local generation is not counted in operational demand [c3].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare EMMS fields for measured operational demand with a separate inventory of non-scheduled generation < 30 MW to see whether their output is omitted from the operational demand field.

possible_explanations.statement: Operational demand might be reconstituted with Wholesale Demand Response (WDR) to ensure forecasts and historical operational demand are comparable, as the document describes [c4].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the reported measured operational demand field and the separate WDR aggregate estimate in EMMS for intervals when WDR was dispatched to confirm the reconstitution process and its magnitude.

It also discusses native, operational and scheduled demand, the three key demand definitions based on “as generated” demand that are used operationally in the NEM.
